title: The Visitor of Harrow Glen
premise: Cyrus Eastwick takes a teaching post in the fog-bound village of Harrow Glen, where a handful of students vanish each winter and no one will say their names. He discovers the school's founders bound something beneath the frost-line — a thing that feeds on the uncounted, sustained by a ritual the founders abandoned halfway through to keep its power for themselves. As mirrors begin lagging behind reality and the frost writes names on every window, Cyrus and three unlikely allies — a janitor who remembers too much, a girl who was almost taken, and the last founder's guilt-ridden descendant — must complete the interrupted ritual honestly, which means surrendering the power it offers. In the end they finish it at terrible cost: the village forgets the missing children forever, but Cyrus chooses to be remembered as the one who stayed.
about_author: Bram Delacroix is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine winters in a valley town that appeared on no postcards. Their fiction draws on chalk dust, frozen fields, and the particular silence of buildings after hours.

chapters.title: The Counting of Doors
chapters.summary: Cyrus arrives in Harrow Glen and takes up lodging above the schoolhouse, noting eleven doors for ten rooms. His POV establishes his habit of counting as comfort. The emotional beat is cautious hope — a man fleeing his own past believes a small school can save him.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: First day of class; twenty-two students enrolled, nineteen present. When Cyrus asks about the gap, the headmaster's smile doesn't reach his eyes. A student, Wren Halloway, whispers that the missing ones 'went under the frost.' Beat: unease dressed as routine.

chapters.title: The Janitor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV shifts briefly to Odell Prue, the ancient janitor, who scrubs a name off the frost-covered gymnasium window before anyone else sees it. He recognizes the pattern beginning again. Beat: dread of the witness who has watched this happen four times before.

chapters.title: Lessons in Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus finds a sealed ledger in the staff room listing vanished students across decades, each entry unsigned. The headmaster warns him not to 'unsettle the valley.' Beat: the first hard choice — curiosity over self-preservation.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: In his lodgings, Cyrus notices his mirror reflecting him a beat behind. He tests it with a dropped cup; the reflection shatters late. Beat: vertigo — the world's rules have quietly changed, and he alone seems to notice.

chapters.title: Wren's Winter
chapters.summary: Wren Halloway's POV: two years ago her brother was taken, and she heard the founders' hymn sung from beneath the ice. She tests Cyrus by leaving the ledger page on his desk. Beat: a guarded child deciding whether an adult can finally be trusted.

chapters.title: The Founders' Hymn
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Wren find the founders' chapel behind the boiler room, its mural showing a ritual half-finished — hands withdrawn from a circle. Odell appears and admits he helped seal it. Beat: the horror of complicity; the adults built this cage.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: Names begin appearing in frost on every window in the village, including the homes of the living. The headmaster orders windows painted over. Beat: communal denial cracking; fear turning inward against anyone who asks questions.

chapters.title: The Descendant
chapters.summary: Cyrus seeks out Marguerite Voss, great-granddaughter of the lead founder, now a recluse. She shows him the ritual's true text: completing it would grant the finishers enormous power — which is why her ancestor stopped. Beat: temptation introduced.

chapters.title: What the Power Buys
chapters.summary: Marguerite demonstrates a fragment of the working: she restores a dead rose tree in seconds. She could bring back the missing children, she says — if someone finishes it. Beat: hope weaponized; the reader wants her to be right.

chapters.title: A Student Goes Under
chapters.summary: Wren's friend Tomas vanishes mid-lesson; only his chair remains warm. The mirrors throughout the school now lag a full second, showing empty desks where children sit. Beat: grief and guilt — Cyrus counted the doors, not the children.

chapters.title: The Village Turns
chapters.summary: The townsfolk blame Cyrus, the outsider, for waking what slept. Odell is attacked; his memory-books burned. Beat: injustice of a community protecting its own corruption; found family tightens under siege.

chapters.title: Odell's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying or close to it, Odell tells them the ritual's final line requires a name freely given by someone the taken loved. He has carried his own name written down for forty years, waiting. Beat: sacrificial love revealed in a gruff old man.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Bargain
chapters.summary: The headmaster reveals he has been feeding the thing deliberately — one student a winter keeps the valley prosperous. He offers Cyrus a place in the arrangement. Beat: the banality of evil; power corrupting an ordinary man completely.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Cyrus refuses and is dismissed, locked out of the school with the children inside. Marguerite breaks her forty-year silence publicly, splitting the village. Beat: righteous anger; the cost of standing outside the law becomes real.

chapters.title: Breaking In
chapters.summary: On the winter solstice, Cyrus, Wren, and Marguerite enter the school through the chapel as the frost writes its final converging pattern. The mirrors show them the taken children, alive beneath the glass. Beat: desperate resolve; the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Circle Reopened
chapters.summary: In the founders' chamber they restart the interrupted rite. The thing beneath offers each of them their heart's desire — Cyrus sees his dead family restored. Beat: climax begins; temptation at maximum, love versus power made literal.

chapters.title: The Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Marguerite speaks her own name into the circle, surrendering her claim to the power and her family's legacy with it. The offering rejects the headmaster, who arrives demanding his due and is taken instead. Beat: sacrifice as the only honest completion.

chapters.title: Under the Frost
chapters.summary: The ritual completes; the ground exhales. The taken children emerge changed and nameless — the price is that the village will never remember them, not even their parents. Wren clings to Cyrus, the only one who will remember her brother. Beat: bittersweet victory.

chapters.title: Amnesia of the Valley
chapters.summary: Morning comes clean; frost melts, mirrors obey. The village wakes lighter and emptier, grieving nothing. The headmaster is gone and no one recalls him. Beat: eerie peace — justice done outside any law, paid for in memory itself.

chapters.title: The Teacher Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Spring term opens. Cyrus remains as teacher, keeping a private register of every name the valley forgot, reading it aloud each night so the record lives somewhere. Wren helps him. Beat: quiet healing; found family formalized in ink and ritual of their own making.

chapters.title: One Second Early
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Cyrus catches his reflection moving a heartbeat ahead of him — watching, guarding, waiting. He smiles and says goodnight to it. Beat: ambiguous grace; the story ends with vigilance rather than safety, and love that outlasts forgetting.
